answer: In the frost-charged lantern of each epoch, agents escrow rewards behind a glacier-thick veil of willow fibers that snap under proof mismatches. A Sybil that forges one fake identity must grow fresh fibers from alpine cuttings; the fiber’s tensile strength degrades 0.3% per parallel attempt, forcing a slower alpine harvest. Every new head shreds another unit of aged fiber, a resource no hydroponic farm can stockpile in bulk, making each extra fake cost a week of alpine labor and a dead willow stump.
